Most footage is landscape: center it with mirrored, blurred bars above and below (Bennett prefers mirrored over black bars). Hook and builder @ sit in the top bar; the account mark (guide sprite / logo on main / dragon on Side Quest) sits small in the lower left of the bottom bar, just above the app's caption text, never over the action and never the focal point. Call adobe_mandatory_init once per chat before any Adobe tool. Upload: asset_initialize_file_upload (path, file_size, media_type) returns a transfer document with a block transfer URL; curl -X PUT -H 'Content-Type: image/jpeg' --data-binary @file to that URL; then asset_finalize_file_upload with the filename and the same transfer document, which returns presignedAssetUrl. The finalize call occasionally fails with 'Anthropic Proxy: Invalid content from server'; the same call again succeeds.

image_remove_background on the presignedAssetUrl returned full-resolution (4284x5712) transparent PNGs with clean edges and no wall pockets between fingers. Output URLs are photoshop-api.adobe.io short URLs; curl -L downloads them. image_select_by_prompt with prompt 'the pink painted fingernails' gave precise nail masks (one retry with 'all pink fingernails, including the nails on the curled fingers in the palm' caught the two it missed). image_apply_adjustments with maskURI and colorize true, hslHue 22, hslSaturation 30, hslLightness 15 gave a natural nude polish; a relative hue shift (hslHue 55, sat -62) came out grey-green and was rejected. The polish reflects pink onto the skin around each nail, so after recolouring, the halo hue was shifted toward skin (hue 19) within about 22px of the mask; darkening that band instead leaves grey outlines (Bennett: 'Nail beds look weird').
Rule: for background removal, masking or recolouring, use Adobe first. Local colour keying is not acceptable for site images.
